narrative: Material PL1__M0A4C270 exhibits intermittent demand (CV=1.26, 62.6% non-zero days) with high day-to-day variability and no statistically significant trend. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=1.17, ranging from 0.07 to 4.43 days), which is the primary driver of safety stock requirements. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy is recommended: the EOQ of 2,147 units efficiently balances ordering and holding costs, while a safety stock of 778 units (up from SAP's 396) is necessary to achieve the 95% service level target given the compound demand-and-lead-time uncertainty.
warnings: Recommended safety stock (778) is 96% higher than current SAP safety stock (396)
Lead time CV of 1.17 classified as unstable — supplier reliability improvement recommended
Demand intermittency (CV>1.0) reduces EOQ model precision; monitor actual service levels closely

research_insights.selection_rationale: Despite intermittent demand, the material has sufficient non-zero frequency (62.6%) and meaningful average demand (332.7/day) to support a standard continuous-review model. The EOQ minimises total annual ordering and holding costs. A Croston-type model was explicitly excluded per instructions; the (r,Q) framework with z-score safety stock is appropriate and conservative.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity of 3,763.741 units does not bind (policy total: 2,925 units = 77.7% utilisation). No capacity-driven reduction was required. Risk is low from a storage perspective.
